reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage xGold participation by linking payment of higher Ethereum commissions and slot activation with an opportunity to make money quickly. Viewers are directed to send specified amounts of Ethereum to a smart contract, with a sampled frame showing a 0.05 ETH wallet confirmation beside Forsage activation tiers. The promotion also includes zero-risk and participant-profit claims, a reported billion-dollar community-earnings claim, and instructions to study the links and act, although the records do not establish completed transfers, actual returns, recipient control, or claim accuracy.

citations.quote: Either paying more expensive now, but then catching this start wave when it is much easier to make money quickly.
In Xgold, it is very simple to activate slots without the website. You need just to send the corresponding amount directly to the xGoldSmart contract.
That is, it is 0.05 Ethereum for the 1st slot, 0.1 for the 2nd slot, etc.
if you buy more than one you must first buy the first slot for 0.05 Ethereum then the second for 0.1 then for 0.2 for 0.3 etc
there is the matrix structure and referral links and the order of payments

opening.argument: The presentation reads as a risk-conscious operational warning, not a promise of effortless returns. It explains that failed transactions still consume commission, warns viewers to verify the activation order and destination, and describes why an insufficient gas limit can waste the fee. Those cautions give viewers concrete information about downside and execution risk. The speaker also distinguishes ordinary network-miner fees from any fee allegedly taken by Forsage. A careful judge should therefore treat the video as transparent technical guidance whose discussion of possible earnings is conditional, rather than deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: Failure is frustrating because the commission from your wallet will still be debited.
make sure to send exactly to the X Gold Ethereum smart contract
the transaction will not take place if the gas limit is not enough, but the commission will be spent.
Forsage does't take any commissions from anyone.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing case treats payment instructions as proof of deception, but the same instructions repeatedly identify failure modes and warn that fees can be lost. Its quoted earnings language is an opportunity claim, not a guarantee, while the presentation expressly calls the alleged effect on Ether a joke. The existence of a payment route establishes an operation requiring fees; it does not establish that viewers were promised a return or that the creator concealed risk.

citations.quote: Of course, it is joke.
Failure is frustrating because the commission from your wallet will still be debited.
if your price is too low, then the transaction may get stuck pending.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings about transaction mechanics do not cure the central solicitation. The speaker still connects paying more now with making money quickly and directs viewers to activate paid slots. Calling one claim a joke does not withdraw the participation pitch. Explaining that Forsage does not take commissions also does not explain how participants receive value; the quoted material leaves the participant-payment structure intact.

opening.argument: The video is best understood as an instructional demonstration of Ethereum transaction mechanics and a specific smart-contract workflow. It explains gas price, gas limit, pending transactions, and the difference between activating through a site and sending directly to a contract. The detailed sequence, including checking success before proceeding, is practical troubleshooting information. Showing how an operation works is not the same as certifying its profitability. The evidence supports a technology and operational tutorial whose subject happens to be xGold.

citations.quote: ForSash Academy has instructions for activating slots both from the side and without the side.
make sure that transaction was successful before proceeding with the next one
What is a gas limit?
if your price is too low, then the transaction may get stuck pending.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument selects the most promotional-sounding sentences while overlooking the video's instructional structure. The speaker explains contract activation order, gas settings, and transaction failures in enough detail to help a viewer avoid mistakes. Even the displayed wallet flow is consistent with demonstrating a technical process. A tutorial can mention a possible financial upside without becoming a guarantee that the process will succeed or pay out.

citations.quote: Then the work of the site was adjusted, but just in case, it is better to always be ready to act directly with Smart contract.
You can set any price for gas
You can check the current recommended price on Ethereum gas tracker.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational detail makes the solicitation actionable rather than neutral. This is not merely an abstract explanation of Ethereum: viewers are told exactly how to send specified amounts to activate sequential slots. The speaker frames that activation as a way to enter early and make money quickly. Technical accuracy about gas cannot change the fact that the tutorial facilitates paid participation in a referral-linked matrix.

citations.quote: You need just to send the corresponding amount directly to the xGoldSmart contract.
That is, it is 0.05 Ethereum for the 1st slot, 0.1 for the 2nd slot, etc.
there is the matrix structure and referral links and the order of payments

opening.argument: The available record does not establish the elements needed to call this deceptive commerce. It shows an Ethereum-based service with stated activation amounts and a technical explanation of how users interact with its contract, but it does not establish a guaranteed return, a credential request, or a completed transfer producing a loss. The speaker explicitly says fees go to miners rather than Forsage, and the discussion focuses on network congestion and transaction execution. At most, this is promotion and instruction for an external digital service; the supplied evidence does not prove the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: Forsage does't take any commissions from anyone.
Miners earn on commissions thanks to which the blockchain is held and transactions take place.
You need just to send the corresponding amount directly to the xGoldSmart contract.
many were unable to activate

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing case infers a scam mechanism from the mere presence of paid activation and a reference to referrals. But the record does not establish that the speaker controls recipients, that any transfer was completed, or that a return was guaranteed. A failed transaction and a warning about sending to the wrong wallet show operational hazards, not proof of fraudulent intent. The claim that a community earned money is unverified, but unverified is not the same as demonstrated deception.

citations.quote: there is known case when a participant attest four slots correctly but then sent several of the following transactions
members of our community have earned more than $1 billion at the moment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of proof of completed loss is not exculpatory when the video actively instructs viewers to deposit escalating amounts for sequential slots. The speaker links that participation to quick money and identifies referral-linked payment ordering. Saying miners receive fees addresses gas, not the source of participant returns. The mechanism is therefore shown through the required payments and matrix structure even if the record cannot verify every outcome.
